about.premise.title: What happened after the report?
about.premise.body: Forms and posts can get a problem noticed. They rarely show the follow-up. Novae keeps the proposal, discussion, response, and outcome together.
about.route.title: Follow an issue from report to result.
about.route.body: Category rules determine the path. Members see status and deadlines; authorized managers can act and respond.
about.route.steps.one.title: Raise it
about.route.steps.one.body: Start a public proposal or private case, or report a facility issue.
about.route.steps.two.title: Take part
about.route.steps.two.body: Support, discuss, or follow its impact where the category allows.
about.route.steps.three.title: Handle it
about.route.steps.three.body: Authorized school managers review, update, and respond.
about.route.steps.four.title: Look back
about.route.steps.four.body: Status, closing notes, and notifications are there when you return.
about.capabilities.title: One place for different parts of campus life.
about.capabilities.proposal.title: Proposals and private cases
about.capabilities.proposal.body: Categories set visibility, author display, support windows, and discussion rules. Private cases keep explicit access boundaries.
about.capabilities.facilities.title: Facility reports
about.capabilities.facilities.body: Report a problem, record how many people it affects, and follow its status and closing notes.
about.capabilities.announcements.title: Announcements and discussion
about.capabilities.announcements.body: School announcements, comments, and replies bring official information and community conversation together.
about.capabilities.pwa.title: Notifications and PWA
about.capabilities.pwa.body: An installable web app with in-app notifications, Web Push, and realtime updates.
about.capabilities.image: Two students examine a facility beside a campus building
about.schools.title: Members see the status. Schools know who can act.
about.schools.member: Members can raise an issue, support it, discuss it, and return to check progress.
about.schools.manager: School managers review cases within category permissions, publish announcements, and record outcomes.
about.schools.note: Novae is deployed for one school at a time and uses Google sign-in restricted to its configured domain.
about.open.title: See how Novae works.
about.open.body: Novae is open source under the MIT License. Its code and docs show how permissions, data, and notifications are handled.
about.footer: A next step for every campus voice.
about.meta.title: Novae | A clear next step for every campus voice
about.meta.description: Novae keeps campus proposals, facility reports, and formal responses on one trackable path.
about.faq.title: What people usually ask first.
about.faq.one.question: Is Novae a suggestion box?
about.faq.one.answer: It goes further. Public proposals, private rights-related cases, facility reports, announcements, discussion, and follow-up notifications share one trackable system.
about.faq.two.question: Can students stay anonymous?
about.faq.two.answer: Each proposal category decides whether the public view shows its author. The backend keeps the verified identity so the case can be handled responsibly.
about.faq.three.question: Who can sign in?
about.faq.three.answer: Each deployment is tied to one school domain. Members sign in with a matching Google school account.
about.faq.four.question: Do I need an app store?
about.faq.four.answer: No. Supported browsers can install the PWA directly. Web Push and background behavior still depend on browser and operating system support.
about.faq.five.question: Can a school change proposal rules?
about.faq.five.answer: Yes. Managers can configure categories, reader access, author display, support goals and deadlines, response deadlines, and comments.
about.faq.six.question: Does AI review or decide proposals?
about.faq.six.answer: No. People write, review, and decide. Automation is limited to notification delivery, data maintenance, and operational reliability.
about.faq.seven.question: Can we deploy it ourselves?
about.faq.seven.answer: Yes. The full project is open source. Deployment requires configured services such as Vercel, Cloudflare, Neon, Firebase, and Cloudinary.
